title: Accelerating ab initio melting property calculations with machine learning: application to the high entropy alloy TaVCrW

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic high‐entropy alloy composed of Ta, V, Cr, and W in a random BCC solid‐solution configuration
recollection.intervention: Development and training of a machine‐learning interatomic potential on a dataset of DFT–ab initio MD snapshots, then use of that ML potential to carry out solid–liquid coexistence melting simulations
recollection.structure: Solid: random BCC lattice with all four elements disordered on lattice sites; Liquid: fully disordered molten phase
recollection.mechanism: The ML potential reproduces the DFT energy and force landscape, allowing long‐timescale coexistence MD to locate the temperature at which the free energies of solid and liquid match, thereby finding the melting point
recollection.results: Predicted TaVCrW melting temperature around 3300–3500 K (within ~±50 K of full ab initio), while reducing computational time by roughly two orders of magnitude

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies an ML interatomic potential and the disordered BCC TaVCrW solid, but incorrectly describes solid–liquid coexistence simulations rather than MTP-assisted free-energy perturbation replacing thermodynamic integration. It omits the electronic Gibbs-energy and SRO mechanisms. The reported 3300–3500 K melting point, ±50 K agreement, and two-orders-of-magnitude speedup do not match the actual reported offsets from CALPHAD, electronic shifts, SRO energy, or 80% savings.
